subject: AtlasMarket CAIQ intake & runtime log sampling request
messages:
From: Alex Low <alex@atlasmarket.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: AtlasMarket Security <sec@atlasmarket.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Jul 2028 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: CAIQ intake: runtime logs + control mapping ask

Hi Sergio,

Thanks for taking this. AtlasMarket is working through the CAIQ for our integration and the assurance team asked for two things to complete our control review: a mapping of Redwood controls to the CAIQ (for controls that touch runtime isolation, key management, and telemetry) and a small sample of runtime logs showing request/response metadata and tenant isolation evidence for a 24-hour window in June.

Specific asks: 
- A CAIQ mapping file (CSV/XLSX) that calls out control IDs and the internal artifact (or owner) we can review.
- A runtime log sample (anonymized) covering June 17 00:00 - June 17 23:59 UTC. We only need connectivity/instance-level metadata, not full payloads.
- High-level note on KMS key rotation cadence (owner + last rotation date) and whether HSM-backed keys are used for private deployments.

Target: internal security review next Tuesday (2028-08-01). Can you confirm owners/timeline and any constraints on redaction or format?

Appreciate it — Alex
Alex Low
Security Program Manager, AtlasMarket
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Low <alex@atlasmarket.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 Jul 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ intake: runtime logs + control mapping ask

Alex — thanks for the clear list. We can meet the ask and I’ll own coordination. High-level plan below and attachments included.

Plan / owners: 
- CAIQ mapping (first pass): attached "redwood_atlasmarket_caiq_mapping_v0.9.xlsx" — owner: me (serving-runtime controls + SLA notes).
- Runtime logs (anonymized sample): Kimberly will produce the 24-hour sample, redacted, and provide a manifest describing fields (launched as "runtime_log_sample_202806_window.tar.gz (stub)").
- KMS rotation statement: attached PDF with dates and KMS owner contact (kimberly_park).

Constraints / notes: 
- We will redact user-identifiable tokens and payloads; the sample will include metadata (instance id, model id, timestamp, tenant hash).
- For private deployments, we can confirm HSM usage in the KMS statement; hosted customers by default use KMS with customer-managed key options where requested.

Next steps: 
1) Kimberly — can you confirm the exact UTC window you’ll extract and whether you need a signed NDA addendum for log export?
2) We’ll share a Drive folder (link below) with the initial mapping and the sanitized log tarball when ready.
3) Proposed quick sync: Mon 2028-07-31 09:00 PT / Tue 2028-08-01 16:00 CET — would either work for you?

Drive (working folder): https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-id-AtlasMarket-CAIQ
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/AM-7890

I’ve attached the mapping draft and KMS statement for your security team to scan; Kimberly will follow up on logs.

— Sergio Alvarez
Head of Customer Security, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Alex Low <alex@atlasmarket.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 Jul 2028 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ intake: runtime logs + control mapping ask

Hi all — I’ll take the log work. Quick note on extraction and artifacts I’ll produce: 

Artifacts I will provide:
- runtime_log_sample_202806_window.tar.gz (stub) — contains CSV of request/response header metadata (no request bodies), tenant_id hashed with salted HMAC, instance id, model variant, region, timestamp, and trace ids.
- extraction_manifest.txt — mapping of CSV columns to telemetry fields + redaction checklist.
- kms_rotation_statement_2027-11.pdf — includes last rotation dates and whether keys are HSM-backed for private deployments.

About the window: you asked for June 17 UTC; we have logs retained, but to keep dataset size small we can sample the peak-hour blocks (e.g., 12:00–13:00 and 19:00–20:00 UTC) rather than every single transaction across 24 hours. Do you need full 24-hour coverage or will representative peak samples suffice for your compliance review?

NDA addendum: we generally do not need a separate NDA for anonymized telemetry, but if AtlasMarket requires a formal export agreement for logs, route it to security-legal.

Meeting: Mon 2028-07-31 09:00 PT works for me for a 30-minute review. If that works for Atlas, I’ll put a calendar invite and link the Drive folder once extraction completes (ETA: end of day Mon).

— Kimberly Park
Security Engineer (Artifacts & KMS), Redwood Inference
From: Alex Low <alex@atlasmarket.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 Jul 2028 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ intake: runtime logs + control mapping ask

Kimberly / Sergio — this is perfect, thanks. Peak-hour sampling is acceptable for the initial review; if the team needs additional slices we’ll request them.

Confirming the sync for Mon 2028-07-31 09:00 PT — I’ll send a calendar invite and include our security lead (sec@atlasmarket.com). No additional NDA required on our side for anonymized logs.

Looking forward to the Drive link and the mapping spreadsheet review.

Best,
Alex
Security Program Manager, AtlasMarket
